_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. status: active = connector-only, a reprint would clobber it; upstreamed = also fixed in the press but the back-port must still be present today.

handfixes.summary: sync injects `select * from <Entity>` (+ minorversion) for the /query endpoint; QBO has no plain REST list path
handfixes.why: Every QuickBooks Online entity is read through /query, which REQUIRES a SQL-like `query` parameter. The generated sync path sent a bare /query with no query text, and QBO answers HTTP 200 with a `{"Fault":...SystemFailureError}` envelope (not a 4xx). The generic extractor finds no array, so upsertSingleObject gets the Fault envelope, extractObjectID returns "", and every resource fails with `missing id for <resource>` (0 rows). Fix injects a per-entity `select * from <Entity> ...` and `minorversion=75` when path=="/query", mapping each sync resource to its PascalCase QBO entity.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press change: teach cli-printing-press to inject the entity SQL + minorversion for QBO-shaped /query endpoints via a sync-hint / x-pp-query spec extension, so a reprint regenerates this by construction. File via /printing-press-retro.

handfixes.summary: sync pages QBO /query via in-query STARTPOSITION/MAXRESULTS until a short page; without it the mirror truncates at 1000 rows/entity
handfixes.why: resourceSupportsPagination() is false for every QBO entity, so the generic sync loop breaks after page 1 - capping each entity at one 1000-row page (QBO's MAXRESULTS hard cap). On a real book this silently truncated catastrophically: only the first 1000 rows of each entity, making ar-aging/ap-aging/dso/balances wrong (not just partial), and QBO returns rows oldest-first so recent invoices were missing entirely. Fix carries the next STARTPOSITION in the loop's `cursor`, sets hasMore from full-page detection (len(items) >= qboMaxResults), and exempts /query from the generic !resourceSupportsPagination and short-page breaks. Verified live against a production tenant: all 8 resources sync to their exact live count(*) across the full book.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Same press change as qbo-query-injection: a QBO sync-hint that emits STARTPOSITION/MAXRESULTS paging by construction.

handfixes.summary: page-item extraction unwraps QBO's two-level `{"QueryResponse":{"<Entity>":[...]}}` envelope
handfixes.why: QBO /query nests the result array one level deeper than the generic extractor handles: `QueryResponse` (object) then the PascalCase entity key (array). Without `QueryResponse` in dataEnvelopeKeys, extractPageItems cannot reach the entity array, returns 0 items, and sync falls through to single-object upsert of the whole envelope. Adding it lets the existing two-level unwrap + single-array-sibling logic pull the entity array correctly. Paired with qbo-query-injection; both are required for sync to store any rows.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Same press change as qbo-query-injection: a QBO response-envelope hint so the generated extractor unwraps QueryResponse.<Entity> by construction.

handfixes.summary: defaultDBPath and MCPStorePath honor QUICKBOOKS_DB_PATH so sandbox and production keep separate local mirrors, and the MCP server reads the file the CLI sync wrote
handfixes.why: The local SQLite mirror path was hardcoded to ~/.local/share/quickbooks-cli/data.db with no per-tenant separation. QBO entity IDs are per-company and collide across companies (sandbox Id "58" vs production Id "58"), so running both sandbox and production against one data.db corrupts aggregates after a mode switch. The Keychain wrapper sets QUICKBOOKS_DB_PATH per mode (.../sandbox/data.db vs .../production/data.db); this env override makes every command (sync, doctor, the aggregates) honor it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press change: a generic <CLI>_DB_PATH env override on defaultDBPath would let any multi-tenant connector isolate mirrors without a hand-edit.

handfixes.summary: aging-delta creates its aging_snapshots table on demand; no store migration defines it
handfixes.why: aging_delta.go (a novel hand-authored command) reads and writes an aging_snapshots table, but nothing in the store migrations creates it. So every aging-delta run errored `no such table: aging_snapshots` on the read path (loadLatestAgingSnapshot treats only sql.ErrNoRows as a clean first-run; a missing table is a hard error) - the command was broken from first use. Fix adds ensureAgingSnapshotsTable (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) called before the read, so a fresh or freshly reprinted DB self-heals. aging_delta.go is a novel file kept whole by regen-merge, so this survives a reprint; this entry is the cheap backstop the reprint-survival doc recommends for novel commands.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press change: novel commands that own a private table should declare it in the store migration set so it is created by construction.

asserts.contains: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS aging_snapshots

handfixes.summary: report pnl, report balance-sheet and report cash-flow pull QBO financial statements (P&L, Balance Sheet, Statement of Cash Flows) from the Reports API, which the /query-based CLI cannot reach; every report takes --columns total|month|quarter, keeps the full row tree and offers --raw
handfixes.why: QuickBooks financial statements live behind the Reports API (/reports/ProfitAndLoss, /reports/BalanceSheet, /reports/CashFlow), not /query, so the generated CLI could not produce them. report.go is a novel hand-authored command group (report pnl, report balance-sheet, report cash-flow; all mcp:read-only) kept whole by regen-merge, but its registration in the generated root.go (rootCmd.AddCommand(newReportCmd(flags))) is a hand-edit a reprint would clobber. Issues #491 and #493 added report cash-flow (operating, investing and financing totals, net cash change, beginning and ending cash, null when the report has no such line), --columns (summarize_column_by Total|Month|Quarter with per-column amounts and column titles from the report's Columns), the row tree (every header, line and total with id, kind, depth and parent, so a group total is told apart from a leaf and QBO's layout can be rebuilt) and --raw (QuickBooks' Header/Columns/Rows JSON through the client's normal answer path and output check). The existing accounts, summaries and metrics fields are unchanged. TestReportRowTreeKeepsTheLayout, TestReportCashFlowReturnsSectionsAndCashPosition, TestReportColumnsFlagMapsToSummarizeColumnBy, TestReportRawPassesTheAnswerThrough and TestMCPReportToolsAreReadOnly were each seen failing first (.review/seen/qb491-493-report-fail-first.txt).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press change: encode the report command group in the QBO spec (or a novel-feature manifest) so root.go registers it by construction without a hand-edit.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For quickbooks the manifest gained: QUICKBOOKS_BASE_URL, QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_ID, QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_SECRET, QUICKBOOKS_ENVIRONMENT, QUICKBOOKS_REALM_ID, QUICKBOOKS_REFRESH_TOKEN, QUICKBOOKS_TOKEN_URL. server.json gained: QUICKBOOKS_BASE_URL, QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_ID, QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_SECRET, QUICKBOOKS_ENVIRONMENT, QUICKBOOKS_REALM_ID, QUICKBOOKS_REFRESH_TOKEN, QUICKBOOKS_TOKEN_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: QUICKBOOKS_BASE_URL, QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_ID, QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_SECRET, QUICKBOOKS_ENVIRONMENT, QUICKBOOKS_REALM_ID, QUICKBOOKS_REFRESH_TOKEN, QUICKBOOKS_TOKEN_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The novel-command acceptance fixtures seed every QBO date as a whole-day offset from the day the test runs, not as an absolute 2026 date, so the seeded books keep the same shape on any future date
handfixes.why: seedNovelStore hard-coded absolute dates (INV-1 due 2026-04-30, INV-2 due 2026-07-15, BILL-1 due 2026-06-20) while the commands under test read the wall clock: the Cobra layer passes time.Now() into analytics.CashForecast, analytics.StaleInvoices and analytics.Aging. Those fixtures encoded a 'today' of roughly 2026-05, so the assertions only held for a 75-day window. Once the calendar passed 2026-07-15 every seeded invoice was overdue, and both TestNovelCashForecastAcceptance (overdue_inflows 800 instead of 500, an empty 8-week window, net_in_window 0) and TestNovelInvoicesStaleAcceptance (INV-2 joined the collections list) failed on the calendar rather than on a code change. This is a TEST defect, not a product one - the shipped commands correctly forecast from the real current date, and the analytics layer already takes an injected `now` that its own unit tests pin. The fix moves the fixtures onto that same footing: novelSeedDay() reads the clock exactly once and seedDate() renders integer day offsets from it, so the books are translation-invariant. The reference day is anchored in UTC even though its year/month/day come from the local clock, because AddDate over a local midnight that does not exist on a spring-forward day (America/Santiago, Asia/Beirut) normalizes back to 23:00 the previous day and would slip every derived date by one. Offsets were chosen to clear every bucket, window and overdue boundary by a wide margin, because fixture dates parse as UTC midnight while the commands floor 'today' in local time - a skew of up to 14 hours. Proven both directions across 658800 (reference-day, time-zone, hour) combinations spanning 2026-2045 over 15 zones including the DST-hostile ones: 0 failures with the relative fixtures, and the same sweep run against the old absolute fixtures fails on 7245 of 7320 reference days, so the check discriminates rather than passing by construction. The tests also got stronger on the way through: the pinned reference lets them assert overdue_outflows, the beyond-window split, net_in_window and which forward week each open item buckets into, none of which could be asserted while 'today' was unknown. The as_of assertion brackets the command with two clock reads (dayBefore before the run, dayAfter after it) and requires dayBefore <= as_of <= dayAfter, both bounds inclusive: flooring to whole days is monotonic over the ordered reads t0 <= t1 <= t2, so a midnight crossing on either side of the command is admitted while a genuinely stale or future as_of still fails.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the acceptance-test template should seed clock-relative dates for any connector whose novel commands take a `now`, rather than emitting absolute date literals that rot. Worth noting for the same retro: no local novel command exposes an --as-of / reference-date flag (only `report balance-sheet` has one), so a caller cannot reproduce a cash-forecast or aging run as of a past date. Adding one is a product change and is deliberately NOT part of this fix.

handfixes.summary: MCP discovery exposes executor-facing request schemas and indexes input names and known enum values
handfixes.why: Issue #351: endpoint summaries omitted required request inputs. Keep canonical JSON body case and nesting, path/header/query routing, and exact short request search terms. Contracts are derived from the shipped CLI source, and the existing CLI commands and auth remain intact. Upstream request metadata fix #4890 was not merged when this surgical repair was made.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Replace this downstream contract extraction only when a released Printing Press generates equally complete executor-facing schemas and preserves every existing hand-fix.

handfixes.summary: config.go composes the company base URL from QUICKBOOKS_REALM_ID and QUICKBOOKS_ENVIRONMENT (production or sandbox) when QUICKBOOKS_BASE_URL is unset; the realm is path-escaped and an unresolved bundle placeholder is ignored
handfixes.why: QuickBooks Online serves every company under /v3/company/<realm>, so the press's single base URL default is a placeholder. Without this edit an operator who set only the realm ID (the .mcpb prompt) dialled the placeholder. It was an unrecorded edit since press 4.24.0 and is now ledgered so a reprint cannot drop it.

handfixes.summary: auth.go registers the hand-written `auth refresh` command
handfixes.why: auth_refresh.go is a hand file; without this one line in the generated auth.go the command compiles but is unreachable, and an operator with a refresh token has no way to mint an access token.

handfixes.summary: root.go registers `dupes` with a literal rootCmd.AddCommand instead of addNovelCommandIfAbsent
handfixes.why: dogfood's command walker does not follow addNovelCommandIfAbsent, so it matched `dupes customers` against the root `customers` resource and reported the novel command missing. A literal registration keeps the surface checks truthful.

handfixes.summary: sync treats QuickBooks' empty result {"QueryResponse":{}} as the end of the entity, while a Fault beside it still fails the resource
handfixes.why: QuickBooks answers a query with no rows as an empty QueryResponse object: an entity with no records, and the page after a book whose size is an exact multiple of 1000. Before this edit sync failed that resource with "missing id" on every run. Tests TestQBOSyncEndsCleanlyOnAnEmptyQueryResponse and TestQBOSyncFailsOnAFault pin both directions.

handfixes.summary: auth refresh sends the client secret and refresh token only over https (or plain http to loopback), never follows a redirect, and shows only the status and an RFC 6749 error code from a failed token answer
handfixes.why: The refresh grant carries both long-lived OAuth credentials. A plaintext or redirected token URL would hand them to another host, and an echoed body can arrive in an encoding no detector decodes, so the answer is allowlisted. Each test was seen failing on the earlier auth_refresh.go. Issue #492 moved the client id, client secret and refresh token resolution into client.QBORefreshCredentials (internal/client/qbo_token_refresh.go), which `auth refresh`, every command and the MCP server share; it still reads them through cliutil.EnvOverride, so an unresolved bundle placeholder counts as unset.

handfixes.summary: QuickBooks dates are calendar days in the caller's zone: one helper set (dateOf, todayOf, daysFrom) drives days past due, bills due, cash forecast, DSO, payment links and SumByRef; report balance-sheet defaults to the local date
handfixes.why: Parsing a QuickBooks date as UTC midnight and comparing to time.Now shifted every aging bucket by a day west of UTC near midnight, so an invoice could read overdue (or not) on the wrong day.

handfixes.summary: every transaction-money aggregate sums the home-currency amount (HomeAmount: the home field, else amount times ExchangeRate, else as written); is-it-open uses the written amount (Money.Open); name-list balances are never summed across currencies
handfixes.why: A multi-currency book mixed currencies in AR/AP totals, DSO and cash forecast, an answer an MSP would bill or chase on. Tests TestMoneyAggregatesUseHomeCurrency, TestNameListBalancesNeverSumAcrossCurrencies and TestOpenRecordsAreDecidedOnTheWrittenAmount pin it.

func (m Money) Open() bool { return m.Written > 0 }

handfixes.summary: query.run (GET /query) is a read in the MCP executor: NeedsConfirm and Mutating are false, and the context tool no longer marks the query resource writable
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 classes a GET whose name is an action verb (run) as a write. Every QuickBooks Online list is also GET /query, and the executor gates any request whose method and path match a gated endpoint, so quickbooks_read refused every list ("resolved GET /query changes state") and the MCP server could read nothing from QuickBooks. Intuit's /query endpoint accepts only SELECT statements, so the endpoint is a read. Seen failing first: TestQBOQueryEndpointsAreReads (internal/mcp/qbo_query_read_test.go) and verify-msp-skills feature 2.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Add `mutation: false` under resources.query.endpoints.run in ~/printing-press/library/quickbooks/spec.yaml; a press 4.34.0 render with it emits exactly these two hunks (plus the mcp:read-only annotation on the CLI query run command).

NeedsConfirm:   true,
		Mutating:       true,
		keywords:       codeOrchKeywords("query", "run"

handfixes.summary: the default local store is scoped by the QuickBooks company (Intuit host plus realm from the base URL) and never by the access token; with no company known it stays the unclaimed data.db every released version used, for the CLI and the MCP server Only a base URL that names a company (a /v3/company/<realm> segment) names or claims a store; any other uses the unclaimed data.db.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 names the default store data-<hash of the credential>.db. Intuit access tokens expire after an hour and each refresh returns a new one, so after a refresh every offline command (ar-aging, reconcile, customers top, MCP sql and search) read a new, empty store and exited 0 with zeros or clean:true. A token fallback for a run that does not know the company also claimed the released data.db for that token, so the next configured run read an empty store. configureDefaultDBScope now passes config.StoreScopeCompany(cfg). Found by the publish adversarial review and Codex round 2; TestQBOLocalStoreFollowsTheCompanyNotTheToken and TestQBOUpgradeKeepsTheReleasedStoreWhenTheFirstRunHasNoRealm were each seen failing first; the generated TestMCPDBPathUsesCredentialScopedStore now sets a company base URL.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: a spec hint naming the stable account identity (here the base URL's company path) so a print with rotating OAuth tokens never scopes its store by token.

handfixes.summary: automatic token refresh (#492): an access token that is missing or expires within 60 seconds is refreshed before a request, and one 401 refreshes once and retries once; each refresh runs inside one cross-process lock around re-read, check, grant and save, so concurrent CLI and MCP processes make one token call; the rotated refresh token, access token and expiry are saved durably before any retry
handfixes.why: QuickBooks access tokens expire after about an hour and refresh tokens rotate, but nothing on the request path read token_expiry or handled a 401, so every command failed an hour after `auth refresh` (issue #492). The press generates request-path refresh only for an OAuth2 spec with a token URL; the QuickBooks spec declares bearer_token, so client.go carried empty lockTokenState/unlockTokenState stubs. The fix: lockTokenState is a real per-client mutex (likelyCredentialed now reads the header through it too); doInternal calls qboRefreshBeforeRequest before resolving the header and qboRefreshAfterUnauthorized on the first 401 (one retry; a second 401 is returned; a refresh whose new tokens cannot be saved fails the request instead of going ahead). client.QBORefreshTokens takes cliutil.QBOWithTokenLock (the filelock.go primitives, with the lock file opened O_NOFOLLOW and refused unless regular), re-reads the configuration with the same --config argument (config.QBOReload via qboLoadArg), adopts a fresh token another process saved, else calls the grant (the one in auth_refresh.go, installed as client.QBOTokenGrant, so its suppressions and guards stay where they are), trying the stored refresh token first and QUICKBOOKS_REFRESH_TOKEN after an invalid_grant, and saves only the tokens (a client secret set only in the environment is not copied to disk) with config.QBOSaveRefreshedTokens: credentials file first via cliutil.DurableAtomicWritePrivateFile (O_EXCL temp in the same dir, 0600, fsync, rename, dir sync), never restoring the earlier file (it may hold a refresh token Intuit retired), and rewriting the config file only when it still carries credential fields. SaveCredentials and config save() use the durable write; the chokepoint gate test lists the two new writers. Tests seen failing first on the earlier code or on a mutant: the cmd/quickbooks-mcp e2e set (.review/seen/qb492-refresh-e2e-fail-first.txt), TestQBOTwoProcessesRefreshOnce and TestQBOConcurrentRequestsRefreshOnce (no-lock and no-reread mutants, .review/seen/qb492-lock-mutants.txt), and the durable-write, symlink-lock and no-restore tests (.review/seen/qb492-store-mutants.txt). TestTokenReadersTakeTheTokenLock (an unlocked-read mutant, under -race) and the environment-secret assertion were seen failing first (.review/seen/qb492-race-and-secret-mutants.txt). A refresh token rejected with invalid_grant is remembered (by digest) for the life of the process and not sent again, so a long sync or the MCP server does not call the token endpoint on every request with a dead token; TestQBORejectedRefreshTokenIsNotResentInTheSameProcess failed on a mutant that forgets it (.review/seen/qb492-rejected-memo-mutant.txt). Codex round 1 (two P1 classes, two P2): (1) a refused token answer's values are held too (cliutil.QBOHoldTokenErrorAnswer, every value but the RFC 6749 error code), so a token named in a 400 body cannot reach output through a later answer that repeats it; (2) the refresh saves to and locks the credentials file Load actually read (config.qboCredentialsFile, recorded in applyStoredCredentials; with none, a --config profile's own data/credentials.toml, else the global file) through cliutil.QBOSaveCredentialsTo, so a profile's next run reads the rotated pair and the global store is untouched; a failed directory flush after the rename is reported; on Windows the lock file is opened with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT and a reparse point is refused. TestQBOTokensInARefusedGrantAreHeld, TestQBOProfileRefreshSavesToTheProfileStore and TestDurableWriteReportsAFailedDirectoryFlush were seen failing first (.review/seen/qb492-codex-r1-fail-first.txt). Codex round 2 (two P1, the first repeating the round-1 class): (1) a refused answer is now held at any depth and under any key, the error member and duplicate keys included, except a string exactly equal to an RFC 6749 code; (2) SaveTokens and ClearTokens (auth set-token, auth login, auth logout) take the same refresh lock as the refresh, so their snapshot-write-restore cannot roll a rotated pair back. Both tests seen failing first (.review/seen/qb492-codex-r2-fail-first.txt). Open (Codex round-2 P2, not fixed): a crash between the credentials-file write and the config rewrite, when config.toml still carries legacy credentials, leaves those older credentials shadowing the new file on restart.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Spec change recorded in the local press library spec (auth.type oauth2, oauth2_grant authorization_code, Intuit token_url): a reprint then generates request-path refresh and the 401 retry by construction. The press template still has no cross-process lock, no durable no-restore save and posts client credentials in the form body, so the lock, the save and the grant guards stay hand-fixes after such a reprint.

handfixes.why: Docs fix approved 2026-11-03, following PR #502. OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand: internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one credkit.Declarations literal (SecretEnv QUICKBOOKS_ACCESS_TOKEN, _CLIENT_ID, _CLIENT_SECRET, _REFRESH_TOKEN and _MCP_HTTP_TOKEN; Files = every config and credentials file a run may read, from config.ReadPaths and each --config and --home; ConfigFields auth_header, access_token, refresh_token, client_id, client_secret; BaseURL base_url / QUICKBOOKS_BASE_URL / https://quickbooks.api.intuit.com; an access token bound to the base URL and the QuickBooks API hosts, the OAuth client and the refresh token to the base URL and Intuit's token endpoint, the MCP bearer and the TLS key to none). internal/credsql registers the one credkit-sqlite driver, with the MCP sql tool's value cap set as each connection opens. credkit.Start is the first statement of both mains, and credkit.Exit ends them. credwire's Files holds, inside credkit.Start, the credentials in QUICKBOOKS_TOKEN_URL and QUICKBOOKS_FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT (cliutil.QBOHoldEnvInputs) and a saved profile's values under a credential flag or base-url (cliutil.QBOHoldProfileStore). Free text is not read: the leak contract's section 1 is a closed list. Every sink is routed: stdout and stderr at the descriptor, the API client's cliutil.OutboundGuard, deliver, feedback, the token grant and the auth probe through credkit.Transport, cache, journal, teach log, profile and export files through credkit.WriteFile, AppendFile and OpenFile, the MCP server through MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP, child processes through RunCommand. The connector's own 0600 credential store and config file are credential sources: their writes stay outside the kit (DurableAtomicWritePrivateFile, cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile). A webhook or feedback URL is its own key and cannot be held (delivery has to send it), so a run profile refuses a webhook value, profile show and use print a stored one as webhook:<saved, not shown>, and no error or message names one.
handfixes.why: Retires secret-echo-decoded-funnel, qbo-oauth-env-secrets-held, qbo-client-success-answers-funnelled, qbo-mcp-success-results-funnelled and qbo-held-credentials-one-chokepoint, replaced by the shared credential kit (entries removed: the ledger's retired list only takes retirements fleet_handfixes.json backs). That filter kept growing per review round because each sink and encoding was closed one at a time. The kit is one shared implementation of the leak contract, checked byte for byte against tools/maintainer/credkit (vendor_credkit.py --check). A match withholds the whole unit, and a credentialed request over plain http or to another origin is refused. Local files the connector writes that carry no credential by construction (lock files, the fingerprint key, the SQLite journal stub) are not routed.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the press should vendor the kit and generate the Start and Exit lines and the sink routing, so a reprint keeps them.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no typed text that could be a credential: the session override is hashed, argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares, a failed flag is a placeholder plus a hash, teach.log records counts rather than raw arguments, and every store of an operator-supplied name, label or operand goes through the credential kit, which refuses a held value.
handfixes.why: The press template stored QUICKBOOKS_LEARN_SESSION raw, and any token typed as a flag name, in argv_shape and failed_flag, with teach and playbook amend writing raw args to teach.log. Unheld, the credential reached those files; held, the kit refused the whole journal entry. Refusal of a held value at the stores is the kit's sink check (no connector-side helper), pinned here so a reprint cannot route a store around it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press template fix; the fleet tool for this class will not merge, so each connector carries it by hand until the press generates it.
